name: world.jobo/developer
title: Jobo Developer
description: Look up Jobo company ids, occupations and filter values while you build on the Jobo jobs API.

tools.name: find_companies
tools.description: Resolve a company name or website domain to its Jobo company ids. Prefix match on the name or the domain (2+ characters). Returns each company's ids, domain, HQ country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and live job count, companies with live jobs first. Use it when the integration you are writing filters jobs by employer: store the ids, not the name, because a name also matches every other company called that. One company has one id per careers board, so put every id it returns into the `companies` filter (or `exclude_companies`). Needs the Jobo API key in this server's `Authorization: Bearer` header; a sandbox key (jbe_test_…) cannot use it. Free: rate limited, never billed.

q.description: Start of the company name or website domain, e.g. 'stripe' or 'stripe.com'.

tools.name: find_filter_values
tools.description: List the accepted values of one open-vocabulary search filter, with live job counts, so the code you write sends a value the index holds. Filters match exactly: an unknown value returns zero jobs, not an error. Facets: sources, skills, industries, company_categories, job_categories, job_subcategories, occupations. `sources` are ATS ids (greenhouse, lever_co); `job_categories` and `job_subcategories` are the occupation taxonomy's two upper levels; `occupations` returns occupation ids for the `occupation_ids` filter. Without `q`: the values with the most live jobs. With `q`: the values that start with it; for `occupations`, `q` is a role name ('registered nurse') matched against occupation, subcategory and category names. Needs the Jobo API key in this server's `Authorization: Bearer` header; a sandbox key (jbe_test_…) cannot use it. Free: rate limited, never billed.

q.description: For occupations, words of the role name ('nurse', 'backend developer'). For the other facets, the start of a value ('pyth', 'soft'). Leave out for the most common values.

tools.name: find_locations
tools.description: Check how a place name resolves before you put it in a request. Returns the places whose name starts with `q` (2+ characters), with city, region and country exactly as the job index stores them, the string the search `location` filter takes for each, and the `{ country, region, city }` object the feed (`POST /api/jobs/feed`) takes in `locations`. This is the free place lookup, not the billed geocoder (`GET /api/locations/geocode`), which this server never calls. Needs the Jobo API key in this server's `Authorization: Bearer` header; a sandbox key (jbe_test_…) cannot use it. Free: rate limited, never billed.

q.description: Start of a place name, e.g. 'berlin', 'san fran', 'texas'.

tools.name: list_filters
tools.description: The fixed vocabularies of the Jobo jobs API: work models, employment types, experience levels, company categories, languages (ISO 639-1), sort orders, description formats and `include_fields`, plus the feed's company size and revenue bands. Use them for enums, constants and validation in the code you write. Values are lowercase and canonical: send them verbatim. Jobs come back with display-cased values (`Remote`, `Full-time`), which are not valid filter input. No API key and no network call: it answers from the filter contract this server ships with. For open vocabularies (companies, skills, industries, occupations, sources, places) use the `find_` tools.

tools.name: describe_search_filters
tools.description: The whole job-search filter contract, one entry per filter: its name, type, the values it accepts or the lookup tool that supplies them, its `exclude_` twin, where it goes in the `POST /api/jobs/search` JSON body with an example fragment, and the matching `jobo` CLI flag. Read it before writing request-building code or types: several filters are spelled differently in the body (`work_model` is `work_models`, `q` is `queries`), and include/exclude filters are nested objects, where a flat `skills_exclude` key is ignored without an error. No API key and no network call: it answers from the filter contract this server ships with.

tools.name: build_search_request
tools.description: Check a set of search filters against the contract and return the exact request for them: method, URL, headers and JSON body for `POST /api/jobs/search`, a ready-to-run `curl` command (bash, zsh), the same request for PowerShell, and the equivalent `jobo` CLI command. The commands read the key from the `JOBO_API_KEY` environment variable; the headers show where it goes, not a value to paste. It does not send the request: no network call, no key, no cost. Sending the request it returns is billed per job returned, and `page_size` is the most one call can bill. Parameters are the contract's filter names, not the body's field names: pass `work_model`, not `work_models`. An unknown name, a wrong type or a value outside a fixed vocabulary is reported with the nearest valid one, and no request is built. Values of open vocabularies cannot be checked offline; the result names the lookup tool to confirm each with.

q.description: Free-text query matched against job title and, unless disabled, description. Wrap a phrase in double quotes for an exact title match; prefix a term with "-" to exclude it. Body field: `queries`.

location.description: Free-form location, e.g. "Berlin, Germany" or "Remote". Look values up with `find_locations`. A string, or an array for several places. Body field: `locations`.

sources.description: Restrict to specific ATS sources, e.g. greenhouse, lever_co, ashby. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet sources). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `sources`.

companies.description: Only jobs at these companies. Each value is a Jobo company id (GUID), a website domain ("stripe.com") or a whole company name ("Stripe"); ids are exact, names also match every other company of that name. Look values up with `find_companies`. An array; one string is one value. Body field: `companies.include`.

exclude_companies.description: Leave out jobs at these companies (ids, domains or whole names, as for companies). Look values up with `find_companies`. An array; one string is one value. Body field: `companies.exclude`.

work_model.description: Remote, hybrid or onsite. One of: remote, hybrid, onsite. An array; one string is one value. Body field: `work_models`.

employment_type.description: Full-time, part-time, contract, internship, freelance or temporary. One of: full-time, part-time, contract, internship, freelance, temporary. An array; one string is one value. Body field: `employment_types`.

experience_level.description: Intern through executive. One of: intern, entry, mid, senior, lead, executive. An array; one string is one value. Body field: `experience_levels`.

language.description: Description language, as ISO 639-1 codes ("en", "de"). Names and locales are mapped server-side. An array; one string is one value. Body field: `languages`.

skills.description: Require one or more skills, e.g. Python, Kubernetes. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet skills). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `skills.include`.

exclude_skills.description: Leave out jobs asking for any of these skills. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet skills). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `skills.exclude`.

industries.description: Restrict to companies in specific industries. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet industries). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `industries.include`.

exclude_industries.description: Leave out companies in any of these industries. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet industries). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `industries.exclude`.

company_categories.description: Hiring company's business model, e.g. b2b, saas, marketplace. Known values: b2b, b2c, b2b2c, b2g, saas, marketplace, e-commerce, service-provider, hardware, agency, nonprofit, government, education. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet company_categories). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `company_categories.include`.

exclude_company_categories.description: Leave out companies with any of these business models, e.g. agency. Known values: b2b, b2c, b2b2c, b2g, saas, marketplace, e-commerce, service-provider, hardware, agency, nonprofit, government, education. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet company_categories). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `company_categories.exclude`.

job_categories.description: Occupation category names, e.g. "Healthcare" (GET /api/occupations lists them). Case-insensitive. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet job_categories). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `job_categories.include`.

exclude_job_categories.description: Leave out jobs in these occupation categories. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet job_categories). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `job_categories.exclude`.

job_subcategories.description: Occupation subcategory names, e.g. "Nursing". Case-insensitive. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet job_subcategories). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `job_subcategories.include`.

exclude_job_subcategories.description: Leave out jobs in these occupation subcategories. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet job_subcategories). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `job_subcategories.exclude`.

occupation_ids.description: Occupation ids, e.g. "esco:8d3e8aaa-791b-4c75-a465-f3f827028f50" or "jobo:backend-developer". Ids, not names: names can change. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet occupations). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `occupation_ids.include`.

exclude_occupation_ids.description: Leave out jobs with these occupation ids. Look values up with `find_filter_values` (facet occupations). An array; one string is one value. Body field: `occupation_ids.exclude`.

min_salary_usd.description: Only jobs whose advertised compensation meets this floor. Body field: `salary_usd.min`.

max_salary_usd.description: Only jobs whose advertised compensation is at or below this ceiling. Body field: `salary_usd.max`.

posted_after.description: Only jobs posted by the employer on or after this timestamp. ISO 8601. Body field: `posted_after`.

posted_before.description: Only jobs posted by the employer on or before this timestamp. ISO 8601. Body field: `posted_before`.

discovered_after.description: Only jobs Jobo first indexed on or after this timestamp. This is the field polling triggers advance; prefer it over posted_after for incremental sync. ISO 8601. Body field: `discovered_after`.

discovered_before.description: Only jobs Jobo first indexed on or before this timestamp. ISO 8601. Body field: `discovered_before`.

search_description.description: Match the query against full descriptions as well as titles. Defaults to true. Body field: `search_description`.

sort.description: relevance (default), discovered_asc or discovered_desc. The discovered orders key on the first-indexed time and keep pages stable. One of: relevance, discovered_asc, discovered_desc. Body field: `sort`.

description_format.description: markdown (default, as stored), html, or the enhanced description (beta) as enhanced or enhanced_html. One of: markdown, html, enhanced, enhanced_html. Body field: `description_format`.

page_size.description: Jobs per page, 1–100 (API default 25). The most the request can bill: every job returned is billed.

include_fields.description: Heavy job fields to return. Omitted: all of them. An empty array: the core fields only, which keeps responses small. The price is the same either way. Values: description, summary, qualifications, responsibilities, benefits.

include_facets.description: Facet counts to return alongside the jobs. Omitted: the API's default set (work_model, experience_level, employment_type, sources). An empty array: none. It is a list of facet names, not a boolean. Values: work_model, experience_level, employment_type, sources, industries, skills, countries, company_categories, job_categories, job_subcategories, occupations.

tools.name: describe_signal_filters
tools.description: The Hiring Signals contract for `GET /api/signals` and `GET /api/companies/{id}/signals`: every filter with its type, accepted values or range and what it matches, which filters the per-company endpoint takes, the focus-filter rule (which types a request with `functions`, `roles` or `job_regions` can return), paging and the two orders (`sort`), what a read costs, and how to poll for new signals in stored order (`sort=created_asc` with `created_after`) so each is read once. A signal is one event at one company, detected from its job postings. Read it before writing code that reads signals: each signal returned is billed at ten times the price of a job, and a signal read again is billed again. No API key and no network call: it answers from the filter contract this server ships with.

tools.name: build_signals_request
tools.description: Check a set of Hiring Signals filters against the contract and return the exact request: method, URL with its query string, headers, a `curl` command (bash, zsh), the same request for PowerShell, and the `jobo signals` command. Pass `company_id` for one company's endpoint. The commands read the key from the `JOBO_API_KEY` environment variable. It does not send the request: no network call, no key, no cost. Sending it is billed per signal returned, at ten times the price of a job, and `limit` is the most one call can bill. An unknown filter, a value outside a fixed vocabulary, a list value with a comma, more than 100 values, a number out of range, a date in the wrong shape, a filter the per-company endpoint does not take or a `sort` other than detected_desc and created_asc is reported, and no request is built. To poll, pass `sort: "created_asc"` and `created_after`; it warns when one is set without the other.

types.description: Only these kinds of signal, e.g. hiring_surge, new_country, leadership_hire. Leave empty for every kind. One of: hiring_surge, new_function, new_country, leadership_hire, new_skill, hiring_slowdown, first_role, new_technology, function_surge, new_city, hard_to_fill, leadership_role_closed, hiring_freeze, hiring_resumed. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values.

domains.description: Only signals at these companies, by website domain, e.g. "stripe.com". At most 100. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

company_ids.description: Only signals at these companies, by Jobo company id (a GUID). At most 100. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

exclude_domains.description: Leave out these companies, by website domain, e.g. your existing customers. At most 100. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

countries.description: Countries the companies are headquartered in, as two-letter codes, e.g. "US", "DE". An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

company_sizes.description: Headcount bands of the companies. One of: 1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 201-500, 501-1000, 1001-5000, 5001-10000, 10001+. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

industries.description: Industries of the companies, matched against the primary industry and the industry list. A value cannot contain a comma. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

categories.description: Company categories, as returned in company.categories, e.g. SaaS. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

funding_stages.description: Latest funding round of the companies, as returned in company.funding_stage, e.g. "Seed", "Series A". An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

founded_after.description: Only companies founded in this year or later. 1800 to 2100. Not taken with `company_id`.

exclude_agencies.description: Leave out staffing agencies, whose postings are their clients' hiring. Not taken with `company_id`.

functions.description: Job categories the signal must be about, e.g. "Technology", "Sales". A focus filter. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

roles.description: Words or phrases to look for in the job title or occupation behind the signal, e.g. "data engineer". At least 2 characters each. A focus filter. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

seniority.description: Seniority of the role behind the signal. A focus filter. One of: junior, mid, senior, director, vp, c_level, executive. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

technologies.description: Named tools the signal must be about, e.g. "Snowflake". A focus filter, combined with skills and technology categories. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

skills.description: Named skills the signal must be about. A focus filter, combined with technologies. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

technology_categories.description: Every tool in a category, as returned in details.technology_category, e.g. "CRM". A focus filter. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

job_countries.description: Countries the jobs are in (not the company's headquarters), as two-letter codes. A focus filter. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

job_regions.description: States, provinces or regions the jobs are in, e.g. "Texas". A focus filter. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

job_cities.description: Cities the jobs are in, e.g. "Austin". A focus filter; only new_city and hard_to_fill record a city. An array; no value may contain a comma; at most 100 values. Not taken with `company_id`.

min_strength.description: Only signals at least this strong. Strength runs from 1 to 100 and compares signals of the same type. 1 to 100.

min_new_jobs.description: Only hiring_surge and function_surge signals of at least this many new jobs. Other types are not affected. 1 to 10000. Not taken with `company_id`.

min_days_open.description: Only hard_to_fill signals for jobs open at least this many days. Other types are not affected. 1 to 365. Not taken with `company_id`.

reposted_only.description: Only hard_to_fill signals for jobs posted again after closing. Other types are not affected. Not taken with `company_id`.

detected_after.description: Earliest detection day, inclusive, as yyyy-MM-dd.

detected_before.description: Latest detection day, inclusive, as yyyy-MM-dd.

created_after.description: Only signals first stored after this instant, exclusive. To read what is new, read in stored order and pass the created_at of the last signal received, unchanged. ISO 8601 with seconds, e.g. 2026-11-12T09:30:00Z.

company_id.description: One Jobo company id (a GUID): the request then reads `GET /api/companies/{id}/signals`, which takes only types, min_strength, detected_after, detected_before, created_after. Look the id up with `find_companies`.

sort.description: The order: `detected_desc` (default, newest detection day first) or `created_asc` (the order signals were stored in, oldest first). Poll in `created_asc` with `created_after` set to the last `created_at` read. Both endpoints take it.

limit.description: Signals per page, 1–200 (API default 50). The most the request can bill: every signal returned is billed.

cursor.description: The previous page's `next_cursor`, unchanged, with the same `sort` and filters: a cursor belongs to the sort it was issued under.
